summary: Someone who promises his weight to the Beis Hamikdash gives his weight in money. The Tannaim argue how to find the weight of an arm.

chunks.en: Someone who says, "My weight is on me to give,"
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate my weight,

chunks.en: gives his weight.
chunks.st: gives his weight to the Temple treasury;

chunks.en: If he said silver, he gives silver.
chunks.st: if he specified silver he donates silver,

chunks.en: If he said gold, he gives gold.
chunks.st: and if he specified gold he donates gold.

chunks.en: It once happened that the mother of Yirmatya said,
chunks.st: There was an incident involving the mother of Yirmatya, who said:

chunks.en: "My daughter's weight is on me to give,"
chunks.st: It is incumbent upon me to donate the weight of my daughter,

chunks.en: and she went up to Yerushalayim,
chunks.st: and she ascended to Jerusalem

chunks.en: and they weighed the girl, and she gave her weight in gold.
chunks.st: and paid her daughter’s weight in gold to the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: If someone said, "The weight of my arm is on me to give,"
chunks.st: In the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the weight of my forearm,
chunks.stMore: how does he ascertain the weight of his forearm?

chunks.en: Rabbi Yehuda says,
chunks.st: Rabbi Yehuda says:

chunks.he: מְמַלֵּא חָבִית מַיִם וּמַכְנִיסָהּ עַד מַרְפֵּקוֹ,
chunks.en: he fills a barrel with water and puts his arm in up to his elbow.
chunks.st: He fills a barrel with water and inserts his arm up to his elbow into the water.

chunks.en: Then he weighs donkey meat, sinews and bones,
chunks.st: And in order to measure the displacement, he weighs donkey flesh, and bones, and sinews

chunks.en: and puts it into the barrel until it is full.
chunks.explain: He then gives that weight to the Beis Hamikdash.
chunks.st: and places it into the barrel until it fills,
chunks.stMore: and the water level reaches the top of the barrel. He then donates the weight of the meat and the bones to the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: Rabbi Yosei said,

chunks.stMore: Displacement is according to volume not according to weight,

chunks.en: but how is it possible to match meat
chunks.st: and how then is it possible to match the amount of the donkey flesh

chunks.en: with meat, and bones with bones?
chunks.st: with the flesh of a person and the volume of the donkey’s bones with his bones?

chunks.en: Rather, they figure out about the arm
chunks.st: Rather, the court appraises how much the forearm

summary: Promising the worth of an arm is different from promising the erech of an arm. Sometimes a promise of worth is stricter, and sometimes a promise of erech is stricter.

chunks.en: If someone said, "The worth of my arm is on me to give,"
chunks.st: If one vows: It is incumbent upon me to donate the assessment of my forearm,

chunks.en: the court figures out his value:
chunks.st: the court appraises him

chunks.en: how much he is worth with an arm,
chunks.st: to determine how much he is worth with a forearm and

chunks.en: and how much he is worth without an arm.
chunks.st: how much he is worth without a forearm,

chunks.en: In this, promises of worth are stricter than erech.
chunks.explain: A promise of the erech of an arm means nothing.
chunks.st: This is a halakha that is more stringent with regard to vows of assessment than with regard to valuations,
chunks.stMore: as one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of my forearm, is exempt from paying.

chunks.en: And in this, erech is stricter than promises of worth.
chunks.st: There are halakhot that are more stringent with regard to valuations than with regard to vows of assessment.

chunks.en: How so? Someone who says,
chunks.st: How so? In the case of one who says:

chunks.en: "My erech is on me to give,"
chunks.st: It is incumbent upon me to donate my valuation,

chunks.en: and then dies, his heirs must give it.
chunks.st: and then dies, his heirs must give his valuation to the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: "My worth is on me to give,"
chunks.st: But one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate my assessment,

chunks.en: and then dies, his heirs do not give it,
chunks.st: and then dies, his heirs need not give his assessment to the Temple treasury,

chunks.en: because a person who has died has no worth.
chunks.st: as there is no monetary value for the dead.

chunks.en: If someone said, "The erech of my arm or the erech of my leg is on me to give,"
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of my forearm, or: The valuation of my leg,

chunks.en: he did not say anything.
chunks.explain: The Torah gives an erech only for a whole person.
chunks.st: has not said anything,
chunks.stMore: as there are valuations in the Torah only for a complete person.

chunks.en: "The erech of my head or the erech of my liver is on me to give,"
chunks.st: But if one says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of my head, or: The valuation of my liver,

chunks.en: he gives the erech of his whole self.
chunks.st: he gives the valuation of his entire self.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: a part of the body that a person cannot live without,
chunks.st: One who valuates an item upon which the soul is dependent,
chunks.stMore: i.e., without which one will die,

chunks.en: he gives the erech of his whole self.
chunks.st: gives the valuation of his entire self.

summary: Promising half of an erech is not the same as promising the erech of half of oneself.

chunks.en: "Half of my erech is on me to give,"
chunks.st: One who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate half of my valuation,

chunks.en: he gives half of his erech.
chunks.st: gives half of his valuation.

chunks.en: "The erech of half of me is on me to give,"
chunks.st: But one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of half of me,

chunks.en: he gives the erech of his whole self.
chunks.explain: A person cannot live with only half of himself.
chunks.st: gives the valuation of his entire self.

chunks.en: "Half of my worth is on me to give,"
chunks.st: Likewise, one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate half of my assessment,

chunks.en: he gives half of his worth.
chunks.st: gives half of his assessment;

chunks.en: "The worth of half of me is on me to give,"
chunks.st: one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the assessment of half of me,

chunks.en: he gives the worth of his whole self.
chunks.st: gives the assessment of his entire self.

chunks.en: This is the rule:
chunks.st: This is the principle:

chunks.en: a part of the body that a person cannot live without,
chunks.st: One who takes a vow with regard to an item upon which the soul is dependent

chunks.en: he gives the value of his whole self.
chunks.st: gives the assessment of his entire self.

summary: If someone promised another person's erech or worth and then died, do his heirs have to pay?

chunks.en: Someone who says, "The erech of this person is on me to give,"
chunks.st: With regard to one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the valuation of so-and-so,

chunks.en: and both the one who promised and the one he promised for died,
chunks.st: and both the one who vowed and the object of the vow die,

chunks.en: the heirs must give it.
chunks.st: the heirs of the one who vowed must give the valuation of the object of the vow to the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: "The worth of this person is on me to give,"
chunks.st: With regard to one who says: It is incumbent upon me to donate the assessment of so-and-so,

chunks.en: if the one who promised died,
chunks.st: and the one who vowed dies,

chunks.en: the heirs must give it.
chunks.st: his heirs must give his assessment to the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: If the one he promised for died,
chunks.st: If the object of the vow dies,

chunks.en: the heirs do not give it,
chunks.st: the heirs of the one who vowed need not give his assessment to the Temple treasury,

chunks.en: because a person who has died has no worth.
chunks.st: as there is no monetary value for the dead.

summary: If someone made an ox or a house holy and it was lost, he does not pay. But if he promised to give it, he must pay its value.

chunks.en: "This ox is an olah,"
chunks.st: In the case of one who says: This bull is consecrated as a burnt offering,

words.note: A korban that is burned completely on the mizbe'ach.

chunks.en: or "This house is a korban,"
chunks.st: or: This house is consecrated as an offering,

chunks.en: and the ox died or the house fell down,
chunks.st: and the bull died or the house collapsed,

chunks.en: he does not have to pay.
chunks.st: he is exempt from paying his commitment.

chunks.en: "The value of this ox is on me to give as an olah,"
chunks.st: But in the case of one who says: It is incumbent upon me to give this bull as a burnt offering,

chunks.he: אוֹ דְּמֵי בַיִת זֶה עָלָי קָרְבָּן,
chunks.en: or "The value of this house is on me to give as a korban,"
chunks.st: or: It is incumbent upon me to give this house as an offering,

chunks.en: and the ox died or the house fell down,
chunks.st: if the bull died or the house collapsed,

chunks.en: he must pay.
chunks.st: he is obligated to pay its value.

summary: When may the court take something from a person to make sure he pays what he owes to the Beis Hamikdash? And the court may push a person until he says he wants to do the mitzvah.

chunks.en: People who owe erech payments,
chunks.st: With regard to those obligated to pay valuations,

chunks.en: the court takes things from them as a pledge.
chunks.st: the court repossesses their property to pay their debt to the Temple treasury.

chunks.en: People who owe a chatas or an asham,
chunks.st: With regard to those obligated to bring sin offerings and guilt offerings,

chunks.en: the court does not take things from them as a pledge.
chunks.explain: They need those korbanos to be forgiven, so they will bring them quickly.
chunks.st: the court does not repossess their property;
chunks.stMore: since one is obligated to bring them for atonement he would not delay bringing them.

chunks.en: People who owe an olah or a shelamim,
chunks.st: But with regard to those obligated to bring burnt offerings and peace offerings,

chunks.en: the court takes things from them as a pledge, even though
chunks.st: the court repossesses their property;since these offerings are not obligatory for atonement, one might delay bringing them. Although

chunks.en: his korban does not help him until he wants to bring it,
chunks.st: one obligated to bring burnt offerings and peace offerings does not achieve atonement until he brings the offering of his own volition,

chunks.en: as it says (Vayikra 1),
chunks.st: as it is stated:
chunks.stMore: “He shall bring it to the entrance of the Tent of Meeting

chunks.en: "of his own will." The court pushes him until he says,
chunks.st: of his volition” (Leviticus 1:3), nevertheless the court coerces him until he says:

chunks.en: "I want to."
chunks.st: I want to do so.

chunks.en: And you say the same about a get for a woman:
chunks.st: And likewise, you say the same with regard to women’s bills of divorce.
chunks.stMore: Although one divorces his wife only of his own volition, in any case where the Sages obligated a husband to divorce his wife

chunks.en: the court pushes him until he says,
chunks.st: the court coerces him until he says:

chunks.en: "I want to."
